SAS PUT(source, format.)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_put.Rd

Writes a value with a format. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

x

Value to format; numeric for numeric formats, character for character ($) formats.

fmt

Parsed format specification: a list with elements name, w, d, char and text, as produced by the translator from a format written as name w.d (e.g. 8.3, z5., $5.). In SAS code this is the format name itself, not a string.

align

Optional alignment written after the format: 'l' left-aligns (-L), 'r' right-aligns (-R), 'c' centers (-C) the formatted value within the width. Default none.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Implements the SAS DATA step semantics (log NOTEs, _ERROR_), which base R has no counterpart for.

See also

Other special functions: sas_f_band(), sas_f_blshift(), sas_f_bnot(), sas_f_bor(), sas_f_brshift(), sas_f_bxor(), sas_f_exist(), sas_f_input(), sas_f_inputc(), sas_f_inputn(), sas_f_missing(), sas_f_nvalid(), sas_f_prxchange(), sas_f_prxmatch(), sas_f_prxparse(), sas_f_putc(), sas_f_putn()

Examples

# PUT: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# PUT formats 3.14159 with the w.d format 8.3: rounded to 3 decimals,
# right-aligned in 8 columns.
sas_f_put(3.14159, list(name = "", w = 8L, d = 3L, char = FALSE, text = "8.3"))  # put(3.14159, 8.3) = "   3.142"
#> [1] "   3.142"

# The Z5. format pads the number with leading zeros to width 5.
sas_f_put(42, list(name = "z", w = 5L, d = NA_integer_, char = FALSE, text = "z5."))  # put(42, z5.) = "00042"
#> [1] "00042"

# The COMMA10. format inserts thousands separators, right-aligned in 10
# columns.
sas_f_put(1234567, list(name = "comma", w = 10L, d = NA_integer_, char = FALSE, text = "comma10."))  # put(1234567, comma10.) = " 1,234,567"
#> [1] " 1,234,567"

# A missing value is written as a period; for a w.d format it sits where the
# decimal point would be.
sas_f_put(NA_real_, list(name = "", w = 8L, d = 2L, char = FALSE, text = "8.2"))  # put(., 8.2) = "     ."
#> [1] "     .  "

# The character format $5. writes 'ab' in a 5-character field, padded with
# trailing blanks.
sas_f_put("ab", list(name = "", w = 5L, d = NA_integer_, char = TRUE, text = "$5."))  # put('ab', $5.) = "ab"
#> [1] "ab   "
